key_insight: V-PaSS improves perovskite solar-cell prediction by encoding absorber alloys and device stacks with physics-aware, semantically rich representations instead of treating them as fixed categorical inputs.
engineering_relevance: This makes extrapolative screening more reliable for new perovskite compositions, unfamiliar transport layers, and previously unseen laboratory settings.
method: Interpolates relaxed crystal graphs of 23 pure ABX3 endmembers using Vegard’s law plus learned bandgap bowing to model mixed-cation, mixed-halide absorbers.
Encodes device architecture with layer order, polarity (n-i-p vs p-i-n), interfacial band offsets, and chemical text via a scientific language model.
Combines these features with tree-ensemble models for property prediction under an institution-grouped evaluation protocol.
evidence_signal: Under unseen-laboratory testing, V-PaSS achieved 2.861% MAE, outperforming a gradient-boosted baseline (3.017%) and the best tuned benchmark (2.912%), with especially strong gains on unseen alloys and transport layers.
watch_item: Performance depends on the availability and quality of endpoint crystal graphs, band-offset information, and reliable chemistry metadata, which may limit transfer to poorly characterized materials.
paper_title: Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System for extrapolative prediction of perovskite solar cells
